First-capture-conditional capture-recapture

Source: vignettes/articles/cjs-first-capture.Rmd
cjs-first-capture.Rmd

drm_cjs() fits a fixed-effects Cormack–Jolly–Seber model conditional on each animal’s first capture. The survival formula models logit unit-time apparent survival. Over an interval of length Δ\Delta, survival is ϕunitΔ\phi_{\mathrm{unit}}^{\Delta}; the detection formula models detection conditional on being alive and surveyed. This route does not estimate abundance or unseen animals.

Apparent survival combines mortality and permanent emigration; this model cannot separate them. The contract also excludes all-zero histories, unknown entry, recruitment, tag loss, temporary emigration, and behavioural trap dependence. A history whose first capture is its final observation contributes likelihood one because it has no post-capture information.

Fit a model 

y <- rbind(
  c(1, 0, 0, 0), c(1, 0, 1, 0), c(1, 1, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 1, 0),
  c(1, 0, 0, 1), c(1, 0, 1, 1), c(1, 1, 0, 1), c(1, 1, 1, 1)
)
d <- cmr_data(y, id = seq_len(nrow(y)), occasions = 1:4, units = "years",
              frequency = c(12, 4, 8, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4))
fit <- drm_cjs(d, phi = ~1, p = ~1)
coef(fit)
#> phi:(Intercept)   p:(Intercept) 
#>      1.99417454      0.02522045

Predict and simulate conditionally

Training predictions return only keyed interval and occasion rows that contribute to the objective.

pred <- predict(fit)
head(pred$phi[c("id", "interval_start", "phi_unit", "phi_interval")])
#>   id interval_start  phi_unit phi_interval
#> 1  1              1 0.8801841    0.8801841
#> 2  1              2 0.8801841    0.8801841
#> 3  1              3 0.8801841    0.8801841
#> 4  2              1 0.8801841    0.8801841
#> 5  2              2 0.8801841    0.8801841
#> 6  2              3 0.8801841    0.8801841
head(pred$p)
#>   id occasion         p
#> 2  1        2 0.5063048
#> 3  1        3 0.5063048
#> 4  1        4 0.5063048
#> 6  2        2 0.5063048
#> 7  2        3 0.5063048
#> 8  2        4 0.5063048

Simulation retains the observed first-capture times, survey masks, and administrative endpoints. It conditions on the first-capture emission and keeps death absorbing. Supplying a seed gives reproducible data without changing the caller’s random-number stream.

simulated <- simulate(
  fit, nsim = 1L, seed = 20261006
)[[1L]]
refit <- drm_cjs(
  simulated$data, phi = ~1, p = ~1,
  phi_data = simulated$phi_data, p_data = simulated$p_data
)
coef(refit)
#> phi:(Intercept)   p:(Intercept) 
#>       1.9745620      -0.2422642

Inspect fixed-effect intervals

Wald and profile intervals use the CJS-specific observed likelihood curvature and constrained CJS refits, respectively. The parametric bootstrap retains every attempt and its status when the original fit passes admission; an ineligible original fit can be rejected before an interval result is returned. Returned results expose a status for each coefficient. These methods have not passed repeated-sample interval-availability or coverage qualification. The current checks report only target-specific single-fit endpoint capability and status; repeated-sample availability and calibration remain open. An available interval does not establish nominal calibration.

ci <- confint(fit, method = "wald")
attr(ci, "target_status")
#> phi:(Intercept)   p:(Intercept) 
#>            "ok"            "ok"

Scope

This example covers fixed effects only. Shared, individual, SD and selection routes remain experimental; extraction-specific combinations and scientific recovery/coverage checks are not established by this article.
